articles.title: PST Sport To Help Fund Artificial Pitch Projects
articles.meta: Sun 20th September 2026 | Announcements | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
PST Sport is delighted to continue supporting North West Counties Football League clubs as they plan, fund and deliver artificial grass pitch projects.

For NWCFL clubs considering a new pitch, a stadium conversion or an upgrade to an existing facility, the PST Sport team can provide practical support from the earliest feasibility discussions through to delivery, testing, handover and aftercare.

PST Sport have delivered over 500 artificial pitches in the past, and are one of only six contractors on the Football Foundation AGP Framework. They are a market leader in Stadium Concersion with FIFA Quality Pro pitches, and specialists in non-league and semi-professional football.

Examples of their work can be found at Redditch United, Oldham Athletic, St Ives Town, Larkhall Athletic, Oxford City and Spalding United.

For NWCFL clubs considering a new pitch, resurfacing project or stadium conversion, PST Sport can provide support at every stage - from feasibility and funding through to delivery, testing and aftercare. Resurfacing projects can be turned around in four weeks with new build surfaces in twelve weeks.

Funding is often the biggest barrier for clubs. Through their finance partner, PST Sport can help identify potential grant opportunities and tailored finance routes to support viable projects. All funding and finance options are subject to eligibility, lender criteria, site conditions and specification. PST Sport finance partner can help clubs identify and apply for suitable opportunities.

articles.title: Week 8: Summary
articles.meta: Sat 19th September 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
EMIRATES FA CUP

Two of our sides were in Emirates FA Cup action this afternoon and we are now down to one in the competition, with Trafford our only remaining side after today's results.

Trafford won 2-1 at Northern Premier League side Heaton Stannington. The Manchester side had the better of the first half and went in at the break ahead after Kyle Worsley scored three minutes into added on time at the end of the first half.

Stannington were level midway through the second half as Max Storey scored at the second attempt after Connor Beard saved his first effort. However Trafford regained the lead on 75 minutes from the penalty spot, Brad Burn the man to score it. It could have been more in stoppage time but for the home keepers heroics, with Trafford seeing the game out to progress.

South Liverpool were defeated 3-0 away at Northern Premier League side Warrington Town. It was a goalless forest half with visiting goalkeeper Dominic Garner keeping his side in the game with a number of key stops. South had a huge penalty shout in the first half though as Neil Weaver looked to have been brought down but the referee waved play on.

Reece Daley put Warrington ahead after 67 minutes at the second attempt after his first effort hit the post, before two goals in three minutes put the game beyond South. Callum Edwards added a second on 72 minutes when he broke through and slotted home, and it was three just two minutes later as he got on the end of a free kick and lifted it over the keeper.

PREMIER DIVISION

Droylsden remain top of the Premier Division after a 3-0 win over Preswich Heys. It was the perfect start for the Bloods with Nellson Van putting them ahead after just two minutes and Jordan Barnett adding a second seven minutes later. The Butchers Arms faithful had to wait until 15 minutes from time for another goal, that being an own goal to complete the scoring.

Nelson remain a point behind after a 3-2 away win at Euxton Villa, that their fifth win from their last six games. Sean Ince put them ahead from the penalty spot on nine minutes, with Euxton turning things around and leading after 28 minutes, Ben Pendlebury with a brace. Andrew Hill levelled for the Admirals midway through the second half, with Sefton Gonzales sealing the win on 73 minutes.

Atherton LR are third, second half goals from Cal Hunter and Joe Bacon giving them a 2-0 win over Litherland REMYCA. A point behind them are Burscough who were without a game, with Chadderton in fifth. They failed to capitalise on Burscough's open date as they lost 2-1 at home to Ramsbottom United. Jack Donlan and Rowan Chambers put Rammy two ahead after just 16 minutes, Chaddy only able to find a consolation through Darren McKnight at the start of the second half.

The biggest win of the day came from Longridge Town who won 6-1 at home to Abbey Hey. There were five different goalscorers there with Oliver Hodgson grabbing the final two goals of the game. Also with a double was Daniel Dolling who scored the first and last goals for Irlam as they recorded a superb 3-0 win at Glossop North End.

The final game saw AFC Liverpool make it ten successive losses as they went down 3-0 at Barnoldswick Town, Kuda Chingwaro with the first and last goals there.

FC Isle of Man play Charnock Richard in the late game (6.00pm KO).

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

Maghull made it ten wins from twelve games with a 2-0 win over Fulwood Amateurs to retain their top spot in the division. They left it late though with the score goalless with 20 minutes remaining when Jacob Till scored. Sam Smith added a second for Maghull four minutes into stoppage time.

Cammell Laird 1907 are hot on their heels after a 2-1 win over Uppermill, all the goals there coming in a nine minute spell in the first half. Fenton Cavanagh put them ahead on 25 minutes with Uppermill levelling, only for  John Lyon to score what proved the winner.

Flixton have climbed to third after a 3-1 win at Garstang. It was goalless at the break before Lewis-Simon Byrne hit a hat-trick in the second half, Garstang getting a consolation in stoppage time. And Thornton Cleveleys are fourth after recording the biggest win in the division of the day, Joshua Winder scoring twice in a 5-0 win at home to AFC Knowsley.

Holker Old Boys are fifth after winning 2-1 at AFC Blackpool, Tyler Spence scoring the winner in the last minute of the game. Ashville won 3-2 at Ashton Town, two of Ashville's goals coming in the final ten minutes. And Woolton won 2-1 at Bacup Borough with both Woolton goals coming in the first 11 minutes.

Steeton won 4-2 at home to Ashton Athletic, any latecomers rueing their decision with three goals coming in the opening eight minutes! Halewood Apollo's first home game in the NWCFL ended in defeat with Squires Gate winning 2-1 there. And Colne won 1-0 at Daisy Hill.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

Sandbach United are the new leaders in the First Division South after a 2-0 home win against Eccleshall. Joshua Fowles put them into an early lead after 12 minutes, with Kyle Foley securing the win four minutes from time. They are two points clear of Stafford Town who drew 3-3 at Cheadle Heath Nomads in a topsy turvy game. Cheadle opened the scoring on 22 minutes with Stafford turning things around to lead 2-1 at the break. Cheadle then hit back to take the lead before Patryk Mazurkiewicz found the net with his second of the game seven minutes from time.

AFC Bridgnorth's nine game unbeaten run came to an end at Brereton Social, an own goal just before the half hour proving the difference. Bridgnorth are three points off the pace but do have two games in hand. Wolverhampton Casuals are fourth after a 3-1 win at Shawbury United, with Eccleshall in fifth.

Biggest win of the day in the division came from Allscott Heath who recorded a fine 4-1 win over Alsager Town. Also winning by three goals at home was Bilston Town as they beat Market Drayton Town 3-0.

Barnton recorded an excellent 2-0 away win at Telford Town, with Dawley Town also winning on the road as they won 2-1 at New Mills. Wednesfield Community were another to have a fruitful away day as they won 1-0 at Crewe, the winning goal being a Rio Tetsell penalty in the last minute.

PHOTO

Today's photo sees South Liverpool and Warrington Town emerging from the dressing rooms ahead of today's Emirates FA Cup tie in front of a crowd of 547.

articles.title: August 2026 paxsport Goalkeeper of the Month announced
articles.meta: Fri 18th September 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The Winners of the paxsport Goalkeeper of the Month Awards for August 2026 have been announced this week by the NWCFL.

The Wigan-based company are sponsoring the awards as part of a three year deal. paxsport are offering an exclusive discount for NWCFL Goalkeepers who use the discount code 'NWCFL' on the paxsport.com website. The discount code is now active on the site and can be used immediately.

PREMIER DIVISION

The North West Counties League Premier Division Goalkeeper of the Month Award for August 2026 has gone to Connor Beard of Trafford.

This is the first time that Connor has won this award and also the first win for Trafford - hardly surpringly though given that they have not been in our league since the 2007/08 season! Connor's performances for Trafford has helped them to win the Club of the Month, with Connor keeping five clean sheets in seven games played.

Connor made the switch to the Trafford at the start of this season after previous being at Abbey Hey, making 42 appearances last season as Abbey firmly established themselves as a Premier Division side. Previous to that he was at Atherton LR, whilst he has also played in the league for Sandbach United.

5 clean sheets, 7 games, 6 goals conceded.

The first game in August saw Trafford host Longridge Town. It was a comfortable afternoon for Connor who kept a clean sheet in a 3-0 win. The following midweek game was less comfortable, with Rambottom United winning 3-0, all three goals coming in the first half. Connor could do little with any, one being a deflected own goal and another a long range, dipping effort.

Another clean sheet came in Connor's third game, marshalling his defence well in a 2-0 win in the FA Cup at Worsbrough Bridge Athletic. When he was beaten, the ball rebounded off the crossbar. Two clean sheets then became three as Trafford progressed in the FA Vase with a 4-0 win at Armthorpe Welfare.

Trafford returned to league action with a 3-0 win at Abbey Hey, that being three successive clean sheets for Connor. Abbey offered strong resistance in this game, but again Connor's organisation of his defence was imperitive.

A 3-2 win at Runcorn Linnets was next in the Emirates FA Cup, Connor unable to prevent either of Linnets' goals. The final game brought a fourth clean sheet of the month, Trafford taking an early lead and being thankful for Connor's form as he kept out efforts from Dean Pinnington and Tomas Brown.

Six games in the month, four clean sheets and just seven goals conceded.

Congratulations to Connor on his Award!

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

The Goalkeeper of the Month award for the First Division North has gone to Daniel Jennings of Woolton. He is the first Woolton player to win this award, and it is the first time that Daniel has won this award.

Daniel is in his second season in the NWCFL and has represented Woolton since their promotion to the league at the start of last season. He has been at the club for a number of years having come through at MSB Woolton Reserves in the Liverpool Premier League.

The first game for Daniel in the month came at Colne, conceding just once as Woolton started the season with a 3-1 win. Next up was a home game against Ashton Town with Woolton making it a perfect start with a 3-2 win.

A trip to Darwen was next, Daniel saving early on from Daniel Basterfield. With the scores at 1-1, Daniel made key saves from Basterfield again, Ryan Cattermole and Nathan Bond to secure his side a point. The first clean sheet of the month for Daniel came next in a goalless draw with Ashton Athletic. Daniel organised his defensive well, and when he was beaten, saw Marcus Cusani's shot come back off the crossbar.

Another clean sheet came in a 1-0 FA Vase win against AFC Liverpool. Daniel set the groundwork with good saves from Aaron Cummins and Kyle Robinson-Murray, laying the foundations for a 1-0 win.

Woolton were then involved in two 2-1 scorelines, with a defeat at home to Ashville and a win at Daisy Hill. Daniel could do little to stop any of the three goals, but made a key save late on against Daisy Hill from Gerry McCullion, fortunately seeing the rebound disallowed for offside.

The final game was a 3-3 thriller with Squires Gate, Woolton coming from 2-0 and 3-1 down. Daniel made several key stops early in the game to prevent Gate running away with it, giving his side the opportunity to come back to force a point.

In total Daniel played eight games and kept two clean sheets, with just ten goals conceded.

Congratulations to Daniel for his performances in the month!

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

The winner of the August 2026 Goalkeeper of the Month Award for the First Division South is Adam Whitehouse of Eccleshall. This is the second time that Adam has picked up this award having won it last November for the Eagles.

Adam played more than 200 times for the Stafford Rangers after first joining the club in 2014, and was part of the Stafford side that won the 2015/16 Northern Premier League First Division South. After leaving Stafford, he played for Boldmere St. Michaels and Rushall Olympic before moving to Hanley Town and then Newcastle Town. He joined Eccleshall last October from Newcastle, quickly establishing himself as the clubs' number one.

Eccleshall started the season with a 3-1 home win against Widnes Town, Adam unable to do anything to stop Josh Quarless' consolation with ten minutes remaining. The midweek game at Allscott Heath saw him keep a clean sheet in a 4-0 win.

Barnton then won 2-1 at Eccleshall, Adam again with no chance for either goal, and it could have been more but for a superb stop from a Joe Keyworth effort.

Eccleshall returned to winning ways with a 4-0 win over Allscott Heath in the FA Vase, a second clean sheet of the season. Wednesfield Community then stunned Eccleshall with a 3-2 win, Eccleshall going three behind there as they switched off for the first hour of that game.

The final two games of the month were both similar. Both were won 1-0 on the road at Foley Meir and Cheadle Heath Nomads, with Adam making it four clean sheets in the month. He marshalled his defence well in both games, being alert when required to keep the home sides at bay.

In total seven games played with four clean sheets and just six goals conceded.

Congratulations Adam!

articles.title: August 2026 Player of the Month announced
articles.meta: Fri 18th September 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The Winners of the Player of the Month Awards for August 2026 have been announced by the NWCFL.

PREMIER DIVISION

The North West Counties League Premier Division Player of the Month Award for August 2026 has gone to Toby Green of Prestwich Heys. This is the second time that he has won this award after picking it up in February 2025 when playing for Stockport Town. It is the first win for Prestwich since Jamie Hill won it in January 2020.

Toby came through the ranks at Stockport County where he progressed to their National League U19 Alliance team before moving to Stockport Town ahead of the 2021/22 season. After two seasons he switched to Droylsden and then Abbey Hey before returning to Stockport Town in for the 2024/25 season. He remained there until they dropped out of the league last season with Prestwich moving quickly to get his signature at the start of this season.

The opening day of the season was one of disappointment for Heys as they went down 4-1 at Burscough. Toby did his bit on the day, winning Man of the Match for his team including an assist for Louis Holt's goal. The frustration continued with a 1-1 draw against Barnoldswick Town, Toby again getting an assist for Heys' goal when his corner was was met by captain James Badrock to score. He also went close to a winner with three minutes remaining, his free kick rebounding off the post.

The FA Cup was next, Toby helping his side to their first clean sheet of the season with a 2-0 win. And next up was Heys' first league win of the season as they beat Glossop North End 2-0, Toby winning his second Man of the Match award with a hand in both goals. The first saw him set up right back Reece Higgins, whose strike gave him his first senior goal. The second saw him convert a penalty to put his side two goals ahead.

Next was another FA Cup game at Runcorn Town. Toby got his name on the scoresheet here for the second game running when he fired in a shot from twelve yards to make it 2-0, Heys going on to win 3-1. The final game was a 1-1 draw with Charnock Richard, with Toby again winning Man of the Match for his performance. After Heys' early goal, Toby went close to a second when he struck the post, and set up several opportunities for teammates throughout the game.

He played six games in total, winning Man of the Match in three of the four league games he played and scoring twice.

Congratulations Toby!

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

The First Division North Player of the Month for August 2026 goes to Adam Smith of Cammell Laird 1907, the first time Adam has won this award. We have to go back to September 2019 for the last Lairds winner, that being Kyle Sambor.

Adam came through at West Cheshire League side Mersey Royal before moving to Vauxhall Motors in 2022. He helped them to promotion from the NWCFL and consolidate their position in the Northern Premier League before switching to Buckley Town. Whilst at Buckley he was named in the JD Cymru Leagues North Team of the Season for the 2024/25 campaign. He moved back to the NWCFL with Cammell Laird 1907 last season where he is now an integral part of the team.

4 MoM from 7 League Games. 5 Goals.

In the opening game of the month away at Thornton Cleveleys, Adam caused the home defence problems all afternoon, leading to winning Man of the Match in the game. He opened the scoring after being put clear and slotting past the keeper, then grabbed his second of the game when he chased a long ball over the top and again slotted home. Lairds were unable to hold on though with Thornton hitting back to win 3-2.

A trip to Flixton was next with the home side 2-0 ahead before Lairds made a comeback. Adam hit the equalising goal when he pounced on a mistake at the back just after half time and slotted home, before hitting the winner with four minutes remaining. This was a cross from the right that Adam brought down before finding the top corner.

Adam helped his side to a 2-0 win at home to Squires Gate next, before collecting his second Man of the Match award of the season in a 1-1 draw at AFC Blackpool. Two became three as he won another Man of the Match in his next game, a 3-0 win at home to AFC Knowsley. There were no goals or assists for Adam in these games, but his tireless running caused problems throughout which his team capitalised on.

The next game in the month saw Lairds win 3-2 at home to Fulwood Amateurs. Adam again impressed, winning his third successive Man of the Match and fourth in six league games. He levelled the scores at 1-1 on the stroke of half time with a superb header, and continued to be a nuisance to the visiting defence all afternoon. The last game of the month saw Lairds win 2-1 at Ashton Athletic.

In total, six games for Adam, all of which were in the league, with four Man of the Match wins and five goals scored.

Congratulations to Adam on a fine month.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

The First Division South Player of the Month for August 2026 goes to forward Nicky Parker of Eccleshall.

This is the second successive award for Nicky, who won this award for Eccleshall in April last season. Nicky is a prolific goalscorer who scored 33 goals in 59 games for Market Drayton Town before switching to Eccleshall at the start of last season. He hit 20 goals last season, helping Eccleshall finish as Runners Up in the league before they heartbreakingly lost in the Play-Off Final on penalties. He has previously played for former NWCFL side Whitchurch Alport in the Midland League, as well as Prees United in the Shropshire County League.

4 MoM from 5 League games. 5 goals scored.

The first game in saw Eccleshall win 3-1 at home to newcomers Widnes Town. Nicky caused problems for the visiting defence throughout and scored the second goal of the game to put his side 2-0 up and give them some breathing space. His performance led to him winning Man of the Match in this game.

Eccleshall's first clean sheet of the season came next in midweek with a 4-0 win at Allscott Heath. Nicky was again instrumental in the victory as he caused problems all night for Allscott. He opened the scoring just after the half hour and added a second before the break. He then set up teammate Levi Hunter at the start of the second half to make it three, allowing Eccleshall to take their foot off the gas a little. Once again he won Man of the Match.

Barnton defeated Eccleshall in Nicky's next game 2-1, before they bounced back with a 2-1 win of their own at Wolverhampton Casuals. No goals for Nicky in these two games, but he did set up Morgan Russell for the winner in the Wolves game just after half time, his overall performance again seeing him win Man of the Match.

Another 4-0 win followed with victory over Allscott Heath again, this time in the FA Vase. Nicky was on target for the second goal in this game as his side progressed to the next round. Nicky's final game of the month came with a 3-2 home loss to Wednesfield Community. After going three goals down, Eccleshall rallied with Nicky's fifth goal of the season getting them back into it, but they couldn't force a draw.

Six games for Nicky in the month, five of which was in the league where he won Man of the Match four times. He also scored five goals in the month.

Congratulations Nicky!

articles.title: August 2026 PST Sport Club of the Month
articles.meta: Fri 18th September 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
We are delighted to confirm our PST Sport Club of the Month winners for August 2026.

PST Sport are a recognised leader in artificial grass pitch construction, delivering complete turnkey solutions for both new build and resurfacing projects. From groundworks and drainage to subbase construction, surfacing, fencing, floodlighting and long-term maintenance, they offer a full-service approach that ensures clubs receive world-class playing surfaces tailored to their needs.

The league have a formula to work out our Club of the Month based on whether games were home and away and the quality of the opposition. Last months winners were are as follows:

Premier Division - Trafford

Winning the Premier Division award for August 2026 is Trafford.

After relegation from the Northern Premier League last season, Trafford have started the season well in their return to the NWCFL. They have played five league games, winning four of them and losing one, as well as progressing in the Emirates FA Cup with two wins, one of which was against a side from the league above.

They started the season in convincing style with a 3-0 home win against Longridge Town. Ryan Brooke scored their first goal of the season midway through the first half with Kyle Worsley and Finley Stanyer adding to the score in the second half. Their first away game was at last seasons runners-up Ramsbottom United, this the only blip on an otherwise perfect month as they lost 3-0.

They bounced back with progress in the Emirates FA Cup with a trip to Northern Counties East side Worsbrough Bridge Athletic, with Scott Sephton and Harry Norris goals securing a 2-0 win. A week later was another Northern Counties East side as they travelled to Armthorpe Welfare in the FA Vase, Bile Ahmed putting them ahead on the stroke of half time. Luke Sephton added a second on the hour with Kyle Worsley scoring the third, before Ahmed secured a 4-0 win in stoppage time with his second goal of the game.

A return to league action came next in what was their fourth successive away game, a trip to Abbey Hey. First half goals from Luke Sephton and Dillon Edmundson put them in control, with Sephton getting his second of the game in stoppage time for a 3-0 win.

The highlight of the month for Trafford came next as they travelled to Runcorn Linnets in the Emirates FA Cup. It was especially memorable for Ryan Brooke, who is the all time leading goalscorer at the Northern Premier League side, and he put Trafford ahead against his former club after just seven minutes. Jensen Bowering increased the lead after 19 minutes with David Worrall making it three at the start of the second half. Linnets hit back and then added a second in stoppage time, but Trafford held on for a famous win.

The final game of the month came with a home game against FC Isle of Man, their first at home since the opening day. Ryan Brooke scored the only goal of the game in a 1-0 win to ensure a solid month for Trafford.

Those results gave them 23 points towards the Club of the Month calculation from their 7 games for a 3.29 average.

The closest challengers were Nelson who have started the season well after promotion last season. Fellow promoted side Droylsden were also up there as were Prestwich Heys.

Total Games played in the Month: 7Total Points won in the Month: 23Average: 3.25

First Division North - Maghull

Club of the Month in the First Division North is Maghull, who have once again started the season in blistering fashion.

Maghull sit proudly at the top of the league at the end of August. After losing their first game of the season, they romped to victory in their next eight games, scoring a whopping 26 goals in the month and conceded just eight.

They started the season with a trip to Darwen with Nathan Moffitt putting them ahead on 7 minutes. However the home side turned it around to win 2-1 with two late goals, the winner coming just two minutes from time.

They bounced back with a 1-0 home win against AFC Blackpool, Jamie Clark's penalty on 69 minutes the difference, before beating Holker Old Boys 4-1 at home. Holker took an early lead with Wil Hoey levelling before the break. Connor Rankin put Maghull ahead just before the hour, with two late goals from Sam Smith giving them the win.

Next came an impressive 3-0 midweek win at Ashton Town, Sam Smith scoring once in each half with a penalty from Jamie Clark in stoppage time being the icing on the cake. A trip to Uppermill was next and they fell behind in the first half. However Ayden Garrigan levelled after an hour with Connor Rankin scoring the winner for Maghull in a 2-1 win in the last minute of the game.

Maghull's next game was at home to Ashton Athletic with Nathan Moffitt putting them ahead midway through the half. However just a minute later Ashton levelled. Sam Smith's fifth goal of the season put them back ahead before half time, with Nathan Peet and Jacob Till securing a 4-1 win in the second half. A third clean sheet of the month came at Garstang next in a 3-0 win. Connor Rankin scored just after half an hour, with another Jamie Clark penalty making it 2-0 six minutes into the second half. Nathan Peet scored the final goal

Perhaps the performance of the month came in the next game at home to Maine Road, a 5-1 victory being their biggest of the month. They went ahead through Connor Rankin on 16 minutes with their opponents levelling shortly after. It stayed that was until just after the hour when a quickfire double from Nathan Moffitt put them in control before Rankin added his second of the game with 20 minutes to go. A Harry Long goal in the last minute outlined their superiority.

The final game came at home to AFC Knowsley on Bank Holiday Monday, with a superb crowd of 455 watching what was a local derby. Knowsley took an early lead before a double from Nathan Peet turned things around, although scores were level at the break when Knowsley equalised just before the break. Maghull secured what was their eighth successive win with Connor Rankin making it 3-2 on the hour.

That gave them 27 points from their 9 games for a 3.00 average.

Cammell Laird 1907 had a good month after their switch to the North with five wins and two draws in their eight games. Woolton had four wins and three draws, with Darwen also having four wins in the month.

Total Games played in the Month: 9Total Points won in the Month: 27Average: 3.00

First Division South - AFC Bridgnorth

The winner of the Club of the Month in the First Division South are AFC Bridgnorth, their first month in the NWCFL being impressive after being laterally moved from the Midland League.

They spoke pre-season that the move to our league could benefit them with more local games than last season, and they have started the season with five wins and two draws from their seven games. They have also done it in style with 20 goals scored, scoring three or more goals in five of their seven games in the month.

Their first NWCFL game came at home to Foley Meir, with Sam Preece scoring in first half stoppage time to open their account. Foley levelled in the opening stages of the second half, but a late double from Suar Dedja - both goals coming in the final six minutes - gave them their first three points.

It was a win that obviously gave them confidence, as a midweek trip to Bilston Town saw them return with a 4-0 win. Kobi Love put them ahead on 20 minutes before another quick Suar Dedja double made it three, this time his goals coming in the last five minutes of the first half. A strong performance was highlighted when Craig Tuckley added a fourth midway through the second half.

The third game was Bilston Town again, this time at home in the Edward Case Cup. It looked like a repeat was on the cards with Mitchell Evans and Craig Tuckley making it 2-0 with less than an hour played, however Bilston hit back this time to secure a 2-2 draw. That meant penalties with AFC Bridgnorth winning 4-1 from the spot. Their first league points were dropped in the next game which was a 1-1 draw at Wednesfield Community. The home side went ahead with just 18 minutes to go, but Bridgnorth showed their grittiness with a leveller four minutes later.

They returned to winning ways with a 4-1 win at home to Crewe, but it was not all plain sailing, especially when Crewe went ahead after two minutes. Michael Williams levelled after 15 minutes, and it remained that way until Suar Dedja put them ahead on 64 minutes. It took a late double from Nehemia Zazi to secure the win, both his goals coming in the last ten minutes.

A trip to Alsager Town was next, with the home side taking the lead before Suar Dedja's penalty on the half hour making it one each. Bridgnorth went in at the break ahead with Sam Preece scoring just before the whistle, and Preece then made it 3-1 at the start of the second half. Another from Alsager just after the hour made it interesting, but they could not find an equalier, Bridgnorth winning 3-2.

The seventh final game of the month saw them host New Mills, another game where they won 3-2 but this time having to twice come from behind. The Millers scored early before Suar Dedja equalised on 17 minutes. Just before half time New Mills went ahead only for Mitchell Evans to level just before the hour. With a draw looking likely, David Anani hit the winner three minutes from time.

That gave them 20 points from their 7 games for a 2.86 average.

Closest to them was Eccleshall with six wins from eight games, with Wolverhampton Casuals winning five of their seven games. Brereton Social also started well with three wins before tailing off as the month progressed.

Total Games played in the Month: 7Total Points won in the Month: 20Average: 2.86

Congratulations to all of the winners.

articles.meta: Mon 14th September 2026 | FA Challenge Vase | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The FA have today released the draw details for the First Round Proper of the 2026/27 FA Vase.

Sixty of our member Clubs have entered this year's competition and 17 will be playing in this round. A further five clubs - Bilston Town, Chadderton, Droylsden, Nelson and South Liverpool - will enter at the Second Round after gaining exemption by reaching the Fourth Round last season.

There is chance for a lot of sides to progress with just three all-NWCFL ties. There is a cracking all-First Division North tie as Maghull host Colne, whilst another all-North tie will see Woolton host Ashville. The third is an all-Premier Division tie with Charnock Richard hosting Prestwich Heys.

There are four opponents who will be facing NWCFL sides for the very first time. Atherton LR will welcome Field Olympic who are playing their first season in the National League System after winning the West Yorkshire League last season. They have started the season well and are in third position in the Northern Counties East First Division.

Darlington Town stepped up to the Northern League two years ago to the Northern League, and they travel to FC St Helens who ran out 9-0 winners on Saturday in their FA Vase tie. Darlington currently sit 12th in the Second Division of the Northern League.

The third is Southwell City who play in the First Division of the United Counties League. Southwell is between Nottingham and Lincoln and they travel across to Wolverhampton Casuals. Southwell have also started well and sit in third place in their league.

The final one is Moulton, probably the furthest side any of our sides have ever faced in the First Round of this competition. Moulton are in the Premier Division South of the United Counies League in 13th place at present. They are between Northampton and Kettering and will welcome AFC Bridgnorth, a four hour, 187-mile round trip for our First Division North leaders.

Other ties see Ramsbottom United also face United Counties League opponents as they travel to the World's Oldest Football Club when they make the trip to Sheffield. Foley Meir's reward for reaching this round for the first time is a home tie with Ashby Ivanhoe. And Thornton Cleveleys, another who are in this round for the first time, will host Northern Counties East side Albion Sports.

articles.title: Week 7: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Tue 15th September 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
After another week of Isuzu FA Vase action, the NWCFL’s biggest winners were Premier Division side FC St Helens. Mike Smith’s side stormed to a 9-0 victory over NCEL side Frickley Athletic, with Joshua Briggs bagging four on the day.

After the game, Smith said: “it was a tremendous performance from start to finish. Defensively we dealt with everything that they asked of us, and going forward we were clinical. The scoreline was probably a true reflection of how we attacked and how many chances we created.”

FC St Helens were the biggest winners, but not by all that much. Further north, First Division North side Holker Old Boys were putting on an attacking clinic of their own. They took the game to Seaton Carew, of the Ebac Northern Football League, smashing their visitors 7-2 to get into the hat for the next round.

Following the whistle, joint manager Kevin Watkin said: “I’m really pleased. I thought the standard of football was really good – the quality in some of the goals we scored, the movement, and it was an all-round positive performance.

“I think the lads worked hard, and it’s important that they take their chances. We got a really good start thanks to Nathan (Reid), and after that we just relaxed, and you could see and feel that from the lads, to the point where we went in 4-0 up at half time.”

Finally, in league action there were more goals to be scored, as Cammell Laird 1907, of the First Division North, secured maximum points on home soil at the weekend with a back-and-forth 4-3 win over AFC Blackpool.

“After getting over the line, manager Glyn Norman said: “We played some of our best football in the first 15 minutes which gave us a two-goal lead. Frustratingly, we allowed AFC Blackpool a way back in by stopping what we were doing so well and gave away two really poor goals. But we deservedly went into half time 3-2 up, thanks to a bullet header from a corner from Lucas Hagan.

“We spoke at half time about getting back to what worked really well in those first 15 minutes and we took it into the second half, by grabbing a fourth and playing some lovely football. Unfortunately, in the last 10 minutes, we again turned the game into a basketball match and Blackpool got a third goal with five minutes left to play, which made for a nervous ending.

“It was a game that should have been won at half time, but left us anxious at the end.”

articles.title: Week 7: Summary
articles.meta: Sat 12th September 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
FA VASE

No less than 24 NWCFL were in FA Vase action this weekend with the action starting on Friday night as Barnton hosted NCEL side Parkgate. The home side were quick out of the blocks and two goals ahead after just nine minutes, however two second half goals for the visitors saw scores end 2-2. That means penalties in the Vase, with Parkgate winning 7-6 from the spot.

Onto Saturday and FC St Helens rewrote the record books with a 9-0 victory over NCEL side Frickley Athletic. Not only was it the biggest win for FC St Helens in their history, it was also the biggest loss for Frickley Athletic in FA Competitions, a total of 247 games! Josh Briggs scored four for the Stripes, with Tom Scarborough getting two. Luke Byron, Michael Fitzgerald and David Ball were also on the scoresheet.

Holker Old Boys were also in record breaking form with a 7-2 home win against Northern League side Heaton Carew. In what was their 60th FA Vase game, Holker recorded their biggest ever Vase score, with Nathan Reid grabbing a hat-trick and Tyler Spence and Ryan Fagan getting two each.

Foley Meir recorded their first FA Vase inside 90 minutes with a 1-0 win over FC Stratford. Foley, whose two previous Vase victories were on penalties, had Finlay Foote to thank for the win with the only goal of the game. It was easier for Atherton LR who ran out 4-0 winners in the all NWCFL clash with Abbey Hey, Thomas Romano getting two for LR.

Woolton secured their second successive 1-0 Vase victory as they knocked out Litherland REMYCA. Colne were 2-0 winners at Northern League side Tow Law Town, with Thornton Cleveleys winning 1-0 at Newcastle Benfield.

Eccleshall progressed with a 2-1 home win against Coventry Sphinx, with AFC Bridgnorth winning 3-2 away at Coventry Copsewood. Ashville conceded deep into stoppage time to draw 2-2 with Athersley Recreation, before winning 5-4 on penalties.

Maghull won 3-1 at home to Club Thorne Colliery, with Harry McNevin scoring twice for Wolverhampton Casuals as they beat Studley 3-1.

Charnock Richard were the other winners, that coming on penalties after a 1-1 draw at Trafford. They had Nathan Nickeas' goal to thank in the 88th minute for the draw before winning 4-3 from the spot.

Squires Gate lost 4-2 at Blyth Town for whom Bailey Adamson scored a hat-trick, with Uppermill tasting defeat in their first ever Vase game by going down 3-2 at Retford. Telford Town lost 2-0 at home to Bewdley Town. Rugby Town scored three times in the first half to secure a 3-2 win against Shawbury United, with Crewe losing 2-0 at CotonGreen in their first ever Vase game.

Northwich Victoria progressed with a 3-2 win at Derby thanks to a late winner from debutant Lucas Edwards. Northern League side Shildon were the biggest winners against one of our sides as they won 5-0 at Garstang.

PREMIER DIVISION

With others in Vase action, Nelson climbed to the top of the Premier Division after a 4-0 win at home to FC Isle of Man. Max Cane and Sefton Gonzales put them two ahead at  the break with Luke Hepple and Billy Priestley securing the win in the second half.

Burscough are second after a 3-2 home win against Chadderton, with Callum Laird hitting a late winner for the Linnets. Oliver Hodgson scored twice for Longridge Town asthey handed AFC Liverpool their eighth successive league loss.

William Procter netted a hat-trick for Barnoldswick Town as they won 4-1 at Euxton Villa, with Elliott Richardson's goal enough to give Prestwich Heys a 1-0 win at South Liverpool.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

AFC Knowsley recorded their first ever home win in the NWCFL with a 4-2 win against Ashton Town. Ben Taylor scored twice for Knowsley with the last of them coming six minutes into added on time to secure the win. Chad Whyte scored both goals for Ashton.

It was a seven goal thriller on the Wirral as Cammell Laird 1907 beat AFC Blackpool 4-3. Ben Wood scored the opening two goals for Lairds, with Liam Owen scoring the winner.

Halewood Apollo beat Fulwood Amateurs 3-2, with Daisy Hill winning 1-0 at Bacup Borough. Flixton scored twice in the final few minutes to secure a 3-1 win at Ashton Athletic, that result seeing them climb to fifth in the league.

The final game saw Joshua Coe score twice for Steeton as they drew 2-2 at Maine Road, the second a penalty in the last minute to secure the draw.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

Jordan Crump and Harry Dixon both scored twice to give Bilston Town their biggest NWCFL victory, a 7-0 home win against Widnes Town. Also scoring seven was Allscott Heath who won 7-1 at Wednesfield Community, Ben Davies grabbing a hat-trick for Allscott with Kian Newnes also scoring twice.

Another big win came at Stafford Town who beat Alsager Town 5-2. Callum Parker scored twice for Stafford with Harley Renshaw on target twice for the visitors.

Market Drayton Town won 2-1 at New Mills, Armando Wood hitting the winner there. And Sandbach United were denied victory at Cheadle Heath Nomads when Jack Higginbottom levelled in stoppage time, Cheadle having twice led that game in the first half.

The final game saw Dawley Town and Brereton Social play out a goalless draw.

PHOTO

Today's photo is from Prestwich Heys whose side applauded their supporters after a 1-0 Premier Division win at South Liverpool (@PrestwichHeysFC on X)

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 6
articles.meta: Thu 10th September 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. The two survivors in the FA Cup

Going into the weekend, the NWCFL had three sides left in the Emirates FA Cup at the first qualifying stage, and two of them were drawn to play against each other. Prem outfits South Liverpool and Prestwich Heys were to go toe to toe, and fellow Prem side Trafford went on the road to Bamber Bridge, of the Northern Premier League.

Trafford did their part, slaying their higher-division opponents 3-1 to move to the next round, but nothing could separate South and Heys on Saturday in a 2-2 draw, leading to a Tuesday night replay. After 180 minutes, South finally progressed, winning 2-1 to join Trafford as one of just two NWCFL sides left in English football’s oldest competition.

2. Seventh Heaven for Glossop North End

Building on the fact that they were a feature of last week’s “Five Things We Learned”, Glossop North End have usurped their fellow competitors in the Premier Division promotion race to take top spot over the course of the last seven days.

Lee Wilshaw’s side achieved this feat with maximum points on Saturday, to the tune of a 7-1 away victory against second-bottom Longridge Town. Alex Bowker and Ethan Sutcliffe both bagged braces as North End stormed to victory. Could this be their year to return to the NPL for the first time since 2023?

3. Nelson ruthless on home soil

For only the second time this season, newly promoted Nelson played a home league game on Saturday, in the Premier Division. Their opponents were winless and draw-less AFC Liverpool, and the home team were eager to regain their momentum after being beaten by Trafford in midweek.

They did exactly that, hammering their visitors 6-1 to further cement their early season claim to a play-off place, and they have now scored 11 goals in just two league games when playing at Little Wembley. Woe betides FC Isle of man, who will be their visitors this coming Saturday.

4. Market Drayton Town didn’t hear no bell

Few would’ve blamed any of the 179 fans who were there to support the home side at the Balufab Stadium on Saturday for leaving at the 88th minute, when visiting Cheadle Heath Nomads made it 2-1 against Market Drayton Town in the First Division South’s three-word-name derby.

However, if they had, they would’ve been forced to digest some humble pie when they got home, checked the score, and saw that MDT had turned it around in added time. Goals by Oliver Griffiths and Durell Manhertz in minutes 90 and 90+2 earned three points for David Lloyd’s side. Play to the whistle!

5. They knew he was trouble…

Widnes Town, in the First Division South, played their first home league game of the new campaign at the Marine Travel Arena on Tuesday. Under new-ish boss Gary Taylor-Fletcher, they doubled their points tally for the season by holding New Mills to a 2-2 draw.

The headline, however, surrounds the man who scored their opening goal on the night, and the minute in which he scored it. Town’s number 10, Taylor Swift, rolled beyond the Millers’ keeper to put his side ahead, and did so in the 22nd minute of the match, for good measure. A true Love Story.

articles.title: Emirates FA Cup Second Qualifying Round Draw
articles.meta: Mon 7th September 2026 | FA Competition News | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The FA have today released the draws for the Second Qualifying Round of the Emirates FA Cup.

Of the 19 Premier Division clubs that entered the Emirates FA Cup this season, we are down to just three, with a replay tomorrow evening seeing which team will join Trafford in the Second Qualifying round.

Trafford's reward for winning at Bamber Bridge will be a trip to Northern Premier League East side Heaton Stannington. They have had a decent start to the season with just one loss from their opening five matches in the league, as well as beating Kendal Town (after a replay) and Knaresborough Town in the Emirates FA Cup. They did bow out of the FA Trophy against last seasons NWCFL Champions Wythenshawe.

Trafford themselves though have had a good start also, winning eight of the nine matches that they have played so far this season. They are in seventh place in the table but have games in hand on all teams above them due to their FA Cup exploits.

It was only last season that Trafford reached the Second Qualifying Round stage when they lost to Nantwich Town, but we have to go back 13 years to the 2013/14 season for the last time they reached the Third Qualifying Round. That season saw them produce a giant killing act to knock out Altrincham before bowing out to Corby Town.

South Liverpool and Prestwich Heys played out a 2-2 draw on Saturday and will try again in a replay tomorrow night to join Trafford in the next round. The winners will face an away tie at either Shildon or Warrington Town.

Shildon and Warrington also played out a 2-2 draw on Saturday and will try again tomorrow night. Both of these sides have had good starts to the season with Shildon in third place in the Northern League Division One with seven wins from nine games. Warrington are two divisions higher in the Northern Premier League Premier Division, and sit in fourth place having lost just one of their opening eight league games.

There is a lot riding on the replay tomorrow for South and Heys as it would open up a chance to make history for both sides. The last time Prestwich reached the Second Qualifying Round was back in the 1983/84 season when they lost 1-0 to Southport. Its a little more recent for South but still over a quarter of a century ago, their last Second Qualifying Round appearance coming back in the 1990/91 season when they lost to Hyde United.

Ties will be played on Saturday 19th September 2026.

articles.title: North West Air Ambulance Week
articles.meta: Mon 7th September 2026 | Announcements | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The start of September marks Air Ambulance Week, the only week in the year dedicated to raising awareness and funds for the lifesaving work done by our League Charity Partner and other air ambulance charities across the UK.

All 62 of our North West Counties League clubs have bright yellow charity boxes where supporters can make a donation direct to the charity. On top of that, they all display posters highlighting the work that the charity does, and all who are at home in the next seven days will be displaying special posters highlighting the Air Ambulance Week.

It may suprise people to discover that the North West Air Ambulance are not part of the NHS and does not receive any government funding, meaning they are funded solely by public donations.

Calls to 999 are filtered by one of the charity’s paramedics and the most life-threatening and life-changing cases that require emergency medical intervention, are patched through to the airbase which deploys their crews immediately.

The charity has three helicopters, two based in Barton and one based in Blackpool – each with a distinctive yellow colour with a blue tail. The crew operates 365 days a year and since the start of the year, the charity has been called to over 2,000 missions across Lancashire, Greater Manchester, Cheshire, Cumbria and Merseyside.

Incidents can range from road traffic accidents, to cardiac arrests and head injuries – and everything in between. Calls can come in at any time, from anywhere within the North West and the crew has to be ready to deploy within a matter of minutes.

The charity needs to raise over £12 million each year to continue saving lives, it’s only thanks to the generosity of its supporters it’s able to continue its lifesaving work. Clubs and supporters throughout the North West Counties League are proud to contribute to the work that they do.

articles.title: Week 6: Summary
articles.meta: Sun 6th September 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
EMIRATES FA CUP

The NWCFL had just three teams remaining in the Emirates FA Cup as the First Qualifying Round took place, and all three will be in the hat for Monday's draw following their results on Saturday.

Trafford travelled to Bamber Bridge who play two divisions higher in the Northern Premier League Premier Division, and trailed by a solitary goal at the break. Ten minutes into the second half Lewis Jacklin levelled the tie, with Dillon Edmundson putting Trafford ahead with just under 20 minutes to go. Bridge pushed for an equaliser and were caught in stoppage time when Trafford were awarded a penalty, with Edmunson converting to give his side a 3-1 win and a place in the next round.

The other two sides faced each other as South Liverpool took on Prestwich Heys. Jack Bentley put South ahead on 26 minutes but it was level at the break with Luke Findlow replying before half time. South then regained the lead ten minutes into the second half thanks to Owen Dursley, and it looked like South were good value for a place in the next round. That was until two minutes into stoppage time when Ellis Richardson found another equaliser for Heys, with a 2-2 draw meaning a replay is required on Tuesday evening.

PREMIER DIVISION .

Glossop North End are the new leaders in the Premier Division after a convincing win away at Longridge Town. An Alex Bowker double put them two goals ahead in the first 20 minutes with Longridge pulling one back before half time. The second half though was one way traffic with five goals scored by Glossop without reply to give them a 7-1 win. Ethan Sutcliffe scored the last two goals to give himself a brace also.

Level on points with Glossop are Chadderton, who won 1-0 at FC St Helens thanks to Jordan Lazenbury's goal 20 minutes from time. That's three consecutive wins for Chaddy now, all without conceding a goal.

Newly promoted Nelson are just a point off the pace after a 6-1 home win against AFC Liverpool. Sefton Gonzales scored twice in the opening 17 minutes to put the Admirals in control, with Luke Hepple helping himself to a second half hat-trick as his team went six goals up. Liverpool's consolation came in stoppage time from the penalty spot.

Burscough are fourth after being held to a 1-1 draw at FC Isle of Man. They went ahead through Caleb Jones goal after just three minutes, with Charlie Higgins levelling for the Ravens with a minute to go. They are sixth in the table, one of three clubs on 12 points.

The final play-off spot at present is held by Droylsden who ran out 2-0 winners in their local derby match with Abbey Hey.

Irlam ran out 2-0 winners at home to Ramsbottom United, with Barnoldswick Town winning 1-0 at Charnock Richard. The final game saw Litherland REMYCA and Euxton Villa play out a goalless draw.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

It was a big day for AFC Knowsley who played their first game at home since coming up to the NWCFL against Ashville. Benjamin Taylor scored their first home goal after just eight minutes with Daniel Bulayima adding to it ten minutes later. Ashville pulled one back before half time through Ben Greenop, and it proved vital with the Villians going on to hit three goals in the second half to complete a fine 4-2 comeback win.

Maghull remain top but wasted a glorious opportunity to increase their lead as they went down 1-0 at Thornton Cleveleys. The Flyde Coats side are up to second, four points behind Maghull, with Ben Duffield getting the only goal after just 18 minutes.

Cammell Laird 1907 are seemingly enjoying life in the North, consolidating third place after a 2-1 home win against Daisy Hill. Darwen and Holker Old Boys make up the play-off spots and are just a point behind Lairds. Darwen beat Garstang 3-2, Kalvin Morris with a brace for Darwen with Kit Lloyd hitting a late winner. Holker lost the chance to move higher as they went down 4-1 at home to Maine Road, Calvin Harper hitting two goals in stoppage time for the visitors.

Ashton Athletic led Halewood Apollo 2-0 after 20 minutes thanks to Josh Nicholson's brace. However Halewood turned it around and hit the winner in the 89th minute through Charlie Glennon. Another game sealed late on was Colne's win at Squires Gate, with Barney Wiggin scoring his side's second goal in stoppage time to give them a 2-0 win.

Cian Donohue scored twice as Flixton beat Steeton 3-1 with Kaiden Barlow also scoring twice for Bacup Borough in their 2-1 win over AFC Blackpool. Ashton Town beat Uppermill 2-0, with Fulwood Amateurs winning 1-0 against Woolton.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

Leaders AFC Bridgnorth romped to the biggest win of the day in the First Division South, a 4-0 home win against Shawbury United making it six wins from seven games. They are a point ahead of the chasing pack with a game in hand on all of them.

That chasing pack sees Sandbach United in second just a point behind, and they had Robbie Hatton to thank for a 1-0 win at Brereton Social, that goal coming two minutes into stoppage time.

Eccleshall are third after a 3-2 win over Dawley Town, with Stafford Town and Wolverhampton Casuals a point further back to complete the play-off spots. Stafford beat Allscott Heath 2-1 at home, whilst Casuals saw Kieran Cook hit a hat-trick in their 3-3 draw with Bilston Town. Bilston led that game early on before Cook put his side two goals ahead, however Bilston hit back for a point.

It was a case of never leave early at Market Drayton Town in their game with Cheadle Heath Nomads. Drayton led 1-0 until 20 minutes from time when Nomads levelled. Nomads then went ahead in the 88th minute through Chigozie Ewelike before Oliver Griffiths levelled two minutes later. Shaun Rowley then made a stunning save to keep Nomads out before Durell Manhertz hit a stoppage time winner for Drayton.

Another 3-2 win came at Wednesfield Community who beat Telford Town. Wednesfield went ahead before Telford turned things around, and it was 2-2 at the break. However a late winner from Tyler Bishop gave Wednesfield all three points.

Barnton led Foley Meir 2-1 but had to settle for a point with another late goal, Luke Lewis rescuing a point for Foley three minutes into stoppage time.

The final game saw Crewe win 1-0 at Alsager Town, an Own Goal the difference between the two sides.

PHOTO

Today's photo is from AFC Knowsley's first home game in the NWCFL against Ashville.

articles.title: Week 6: Preview
articles.meta: Fri 4th September 2026 | Match Previews | By Ben Wilkinson
articles.body:
PREMIER DIVISION

Charnock Richard vs Barnoldswick TownCharnock Richard come into the weekend in 9th position and are now unbeaten in their last three, while Barnoldswick sit in 13th with as many as five draws to their name already this term. Charnock seem to have Barlick's number, winning 14 of the 18 games between the pair! The visitors from East Lancashire will aim to buck the trend and secure a first win at Mossie Park since February 2018.

Droylsden vs Abbey HeyIt's a local derby at the Butchers' Arms where Droylsden welcome rivals Abbey Hey. The Bloods started the season off well but have lost two of their last three in all competitions, whilst Abbey Hey have yet to taste victory this season and have shipped six goals in a game on no fewer than three occasions already.

FC St Helens vs ChaddertonFC St Helens have had a middling start to the campaign and lie in 12th position, whilst the visitors Chadderton are in 2nd place in their mission to push on after positive seasons since their own promotion. The Stripes had kept four clean sheets in a row before defeat against Charnock Richard midweek and they will need that defensive stability on home soil against an attacking Chady outfit.

Irlam vs Ramsbottom UnitedRamsbottom make the journey round the M60 to Silver Street to take on Irlam on Saturday afternoon. Rammy have had an inconsistent start to life under Rob Henry's premiership but two wins on the bounce suggests that a corner may have been turned as they look to go one better than last time and secure a return to the NPL.

Nelson vs AFC LiverpoolAFC Liverpool have suffered a torrid start to their 2026/27 season, having lost every game to date and as a result they remain rooted to the foot of the table. It's a tall ask for them to turn it around this weekend as they visit The Daisy Arena to face a very impressive Nelson side, who sit 4th in the table with four wins from their opening six. The Admirals, under the stewardship of Arron Ripley, have made a storming start to life in the Premier Division and will see this as a great opportunity to return to winning ways following a narrow reverse against Trafford last time out.

FC Isle of Man vs BurscoughIt's been a positive start to the season for FC Isle of Man after their struggles last time out and they are currently in 7th position, whilst this weekend's visitors to The Bowl, Burscough, sit pretty at the top of the tree and have hit the back of the net 22 times already this term! This is arguably the standout fixture in the Premier Division this weekend with two attacking sides going tooth and nail on Saturday evening.

Other fixtures:

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

AFC Knowsley vs AshvilleIt's a long awaited first NWCFL home game for AFC Knowsley and they come into this momentous occasion with 7 points from their opening 8 games (all away from home). The first visitors to the Lord Derby Pavilion are Ashville, who with a record of 3-3-3 from their 9 games to date are the definition of consistently inconsistent! Ashville's last game was their first of the season where they kept a clean sheet, whilst they have scored in every match-up so far - expect more goals here!

Ashton Town vs UppermillUppermill have struggled following promotion and currently bring up the rear of the pack with just three points and no wins. Their hosts on Saturday started in similar fashion, losing their opening six, before three wins on the bounce propelled them up the table. With another home game here, Town will be aiming to make it four and further compound Uppermill's miserable opening to life on the pitch in the NWCFL.

Darwen FC vs GarstangTwo Lancastrian sides with opposing starts to the season do battle at the Anchor Ground. Hosts Darwen have taken 14 points from their 7 games and lie just outside the playoff spots whilst Garstang look set for another season of struggle after picking up just four points so far. The Salmoners have notched 11 times in their last four and will seek to keep that firepower up front active.

Flixton vs SteetonIt's a first ever competitive meeting between these two as Steeton make the journey over to Manchester to take on Flixton at Valley Road. The league table would make the hosts firm favourites but the visiting Chevvies are more than capable of turning on the style and upsetting the applecart on their day.

Fulwood Amateurs vs WooltonFulwood, despite scoring 11 in their last four, haven't taken the win in any of them as a leaky defence has proved their undoing thus far whilst their opponents on Saturday boast one of the meanest back lines in the division with 10 goals conceded and just one defeat. Fulwood's home advantage may prove to be the difference in a finely-poised encounter.

Ashton Athletic vs Halewood ApolloHalewood Apollo attempt to return to winning ways away at an Ashton Athletic side who are reeling from five successive defeats. Athletic started the season strongly with two wins to nil but are now on a run of seven without success. There's been 29 goals in the 8 league games involving Apollo so form would say this is unlikely to be a dull affair.

Holker Old Boys vs Maine RoadHolker Old Boys lead the chasing pack and thrice came back from two goals down to snatch a draw away at Fulwood Amateurs during the week, next up for them is Maine Road, who make the long trip up to Barrow this weekend. The Brantingham Road side have struggled of late and haven't tasted victory since 11th August; three defeats and a draw since see them in 19th place at this stage.

Thornton Cleveleys vs MaghullMaghull are already an incredible seven points clear after a thunderous start featuring eight wins out of a possible nine. Next in their path is a Thornton Cleveleys side who harbour promotion aspirations of their own and will look to keep a place in the top five throughout the season. These two can't be separated on head-to-head record, with two wins apiece joined by a draw in the two seasons these two have locked horns - including 5-2 victories for both!

Other fixtures:
